newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol outstrips indices amid strong demand.
newsitem.headline: Repsol outstrips indices amid strong demand.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Repsol were strongly higher on Wednesday, buoyed by foreign-investor buying on reports that the retail tranche is going well, dealers said.

The government is selling its last 10.00 percent stake in the energy firm this month, and the period for provisional orders from small shareholders started on Monday. Press reports said the offer is so far oversubscribed twice for that tranche.
In view of this, dealers said it seemed likely the lead managers could increase the retail segment, set at an initial 12.75 million shares.
At 1100 GMT, Repsol was up 80 pesetas, of 1.33 percent, to 6,090 pesetas, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up 0.75 percent to 5,523.83.

"More or less everyone is buying, but foreign investors are particularly keen because the stock is liquid enough for them to buy it now on the market rather than wait for the placement," said a dealer who requested anonymity.

"I wouldn't be at all surprised if they increased the retail tranche again. But the news about retail subcriptions should be taken with a pinch of salt because of the design of the placement," he added.
Aiming to avoid investor frustration, lead managers are to provide would-be shareholders with an estimate of how many shares they are likely to be allocated when they make a provisional order.
This way they can decide if it will be worth their while to make their order definitive if the offer is heavily subscribed, and the final allocation thus limited.
But dealers said this method may mean that small shareholders initially bid for more shares than they actually want, exaggerating the success of the placement.
